_notes: Per-pair curated data. Most fields are derivable from zones.json and don't need to be stored here (time difference, DST relationship, etc. — compute at template render time). This file holds only the curated content that can't be derived: meeting overlap recommendations, sample city pairs, notable pairing context, flight times, and meeting difficulty assessment. Examples below cover all five DST-relationship variants. Target is ~250 P1 directional pairs across all 25 zones.

_pair_categories.synchronized: Both zones observe DST on the same schedule. Differential is constant year-round. Example: any two US zones (EST↔PST, CST↔MST). Easiest case for templates.
_pair_categories.desynchronized: Both zones observe DST but on different schedules (US vs EU). Differential shifts during the 2-3 weeks per year when one zone has switched and the other hasn't. Example: EST↔CET.
_pair_categories.asymmetric: One zone observes DST, the other doesn't. Differential shifts twice a year by 1 hour. Examples: EST↔IST, CET↔IST, PST↔JST.
_pair_categories.inverted: Both zones observe DST but on opposite-season schedules (Northern vs Southern Hemisphere). When one springs forward, the other falls back. The time difference shifts twice a year, like 'desynchronized', but the shift pattern is opposite-season rather than schedule-misalignment. Examples: EST↔AEDT, CET↔NZDT, PST↔AEDT. Distinct from 'desynchronized' which is same-season but schedule-mistimed (US↔EU).
_pair_categories.neither: Neither zone observes DST. Differential is constant year-round. Example: IST↔JST, HST↔IST, UTC↔IST.

_field_definitions.source_code: Source zone code (e.g., 'EST'). Must match a zone in zones.json.
_field_definitions.target_code: Target zone code. Must match a zone in zones.json.
_field_definitions.dst_relationship: One of: synchronized, desynchronized, asymmetric, inverted, neither. Used by the template to select content variants.
_field_definitions.sample_source_city: Specific city to feature for this source zone in this pair's context (e.g., 'New York' for EST, 'Mumbai' for IST). Should be the most recognized city for the relevant business context.
_field_definitions.meeting_overlap: Object with start/end times in both zones. Curated recommendation, not derived. Should respect 9-5 working hours in both zones where possible; for difficult pairs, recommend the closest workable window.
_field_definitions.meeting_difficulty: One of: easy, moderate, hard. Easy = full overlap in business hours. Moderate = partial overlap. Hard = no overlap; teams typically use async or bridge calls.
_field_definitions.notable_pairing: 1-2 sentences of context: who works across these zones and how. This is the most genuinely unique content per pair.
_field_definitions.flight_route: Object with hub airports, average flight time in minutes, and direct flight availability. Optional but recommended.
_field_definitions.common_use_cases: Array of 2-4 strings describing typical reasons users convert this pair (e.g., 'business meetings', 'flight scheduling', 'family abroad', 'remote work coordination').

pairs.notable_pairing: UTC↔EST is the most-converted pair for developers and technical teams, since most servers, log files, and APIs run on UTC and most US business operates on EST. Calendar bugs around DST transitions are a frequent source of incidents in software systems.

pairs._variant: INVERTED — both observe DST on opposite-hemisphere schedules

meeting_overlap.note: The gap is 15 hours when both zones are in standard time (US winter / AU summer is impossible simultaneously — by definition), and shifts as each hemisphere changes clocks. In practice: when EST is UTC-5 (US winter, AU is in AEDT/UTC+11), the gap is 16 hours. When EDT is active (US summer, AU is in AEST/UTC+10), the gap is 14 hours. The workable live-meeting window — early morning New York / late evening Sydney — is genuinely narrow and most US-Australia business is conducted asynchronously.

pairs.notable_pairing: The US East Coast to Australia corridor is one of the most search-heavy long-haul time zone pairs. Finance, technology, and media companies with operations in both New York and Sydney typically schedule a weekly bridge call in the narrow overlap window or rely entirely on async hand-offs. The opposite-hemisphere DST patterns mean the gap shifts four times per year rather than the two times seen in same-hemisphere desynchronized pairs.

flight_route.note: No direct service from JFK to Sydney exists; typical routing is via LAX (Qantas QF12) for a total journey of 21+ hours. LAX↔SYD is one of the longest non-stop commercial routes in the world at roughly 15 hours.
